title: SAT Rhetorical Synthesis: How to Ace the Notes Questions
description:
SAT rhetorical synthesis questions (the "notes" questions) give you a list of bulleted notes and a goal, then ask which sentence uses the notes to accomplish that goal. Almost every choice is accurate, so accuracy isn't what decides the answer. The goal is. This video shows how to read the goal first, turn it into a checklist, and work through six SAT-style questions.

You'll learn:
• What a rhetorical synthesis question looks like and what it's really testing
• Common goals: similarity, difference, an unfamiliar audience, a study and its findings, an advantage
• The four traps: true but off goal, right type but wrong detail, half the goal, and one side only
• How to handle a two-part goal (the hardest version)

All practice questions in this video are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (filter: Expression of Ideas, Rhetorical Synthesis).
